title: Dispatch console actions with audit trail
name: Dispatch audit trail

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code makes sure privileged dispatch actions are recorded in the audit log? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A user with the dispatcher role calls suspend_driver. What is left behind in the database?
choices: Nothing, because the exception is raised before any state is written.
An access.denied audit entry naming the caller and the attempted action; the driver is unchanged.
A driver.suspended audit entry with a failed outcome flag.
The driver is suspended, and an access.denied entry is written afterwards.

questions.prompt: Why does suspend_driver load the driver with with_for_update=True before reading previous = driver.status?
choices: It makes the session flush the status change immediately instead of at commit.
It lets the ORM skip the SELECT when the driver is already in the session.
It guarantees the audit entry is written even if the commit later fails.
It locks the row so the previous status stored in the audit detail cannot be changed by a concurrent transaction before this one commits.

questions.prompt: In suspend_driver, the database connection drops while session.commit() is executing and the transaction is rolled back. What does the audit table contain for this request?
choices: No driver.suspended entry, because the entry was added to the same session and transaction as the status change.
A driver.suspended entry, because audit rows are flushed as soon as add() is called.
A driver.suspended entry marked as pending, which a background job later reconciles.
Both the entry and the new status, because commit is retried by SQLAlchemy.
